pull_request.title: Tracker: Test transverse pixel periphery and close z packing
pull_request.head: study/pixel-z-coverage
pull_request.body:
Move the inherited pixel readout periphery into r–phi and test close module packing along z, without changing the current DD4hep default. DES-013 is an isolated prototype for eventual expert approval; it preserves barrel radii/stave counts, pixel endcaps and strips.

Recommend the **chip-centred 0.2 mm sensor-edge / 0.2 mm body-gap** hypothesis for engineering review. The active inter-module z gap becomes 0.6 mm; quad internal 0.2 mm readout seams remain inactive.

| Matched off-grid metric | Baseline | Proposed target |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Missed reachable barrel layers, straight | 16.54% | 3.87% |
| Missed layers, 1 GeV pT / 3 T, q+ | 16.43% | 3.86% |
| Missed layers, 1 GeV pT / 3 T, q− | 16.65% | 4.01% |
| All reachable barrel layers hit, straight | 59.02% | 88.62% |
| Modules / ASICs | 2,750 / 6,206 | 3,050 / 6,794 |
| Pixel-barrel sensor area | 2.5574 m² | 2.7491 m² |
| Nominal ASIC power | 16.6817 kW | 18.2623 kW |

These are sampled geometric fractions, not event efficiencies or proof of hermeticity. Six cases separate rotation, packing, edge width and common row phase. A symmetric quad phase loses two central barrel stations; chip-centred packing restores four on those probes. A 0.5 mm edge control has a four-layer aligned hole at z=−11 mm, confirmed with ACTS. The aggressive 0.1 mm option improves the missing fraction by less than one further percentage point.

**Cooling amendment required:** inherited quad flow gives stress exit quality 0.45705 against the 0.45 ceiling; single staves have almost no margin. The failure is retained. The report derives a minimum quad heat-balance flow and proposes further thermal/hydraulic and cable-capacity work; it does not change the cooling baseline or certify assembly tolerances, guards or bond geometry.

Review entry points:
- [DES-013 design and provenance](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/pixel-z-coverage/docs/design/DES-013-pixel-barrel-z-coverage.md), linked to module issue #7 and DES-002/011/012.
- [Results and all per-layer/subdetector tables](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/pixel-z-coverage/docs/validation/DES-013-pixel-z/results.md).
- [Recommendation, limitations and cooling amendment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/pixel-z-coverage/docs/validation/DES-013-pixel-z/recommendation.md).
- [Repeatable workflow](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/study/pixel-z-coverage/tools/pixel_z_coverage/README.md), including future shape updates, native setup and lossless evidence archiving.
- Module-orientation and luminous-z seam SVGs accompany the report; complete layouts, per-track counts, configuration and runtime/source fingerprints are retained.

Validation executed:
- Six cases × 7,312 matched primary rays × 3 modes; separate 4,096-ray total-p=1 GeV sensitivity for both charges. Luminous box x/y ∈ [0,1] mm, z ∈ [−150,150] mm; |eta| ≤ 4.
- **720 native ACTS track audits pass**, including explicit 1 µm inside/outside sensor-edge controls. Finite supporting-plane propagation and native bounds, not global navigator/reconstruction validation.
- Zero occupied-body or outward-support envelope conflicts. Unchanged regions retain identical primary per-track counts.
- 6 layout tests, 15 intersection tests, 3 native integration controls and 27 dashboard tests pass; dashboard validation/build and session-log validation pass.
- Actual ACTS/ROOT runtime verified despite stale Spack registry fingerprints. No shared dependencies modified; the binding overlay's reused-build provenance remains explicit.

No formal sign-off or baseline adoption is inferred. This PR supplies evidence for that decision.

issues.title: Design reusable RD53 pixel-module alternatives
issues.body:
Develop DES-001 as a stand-alone RD53 pixel-module proposal with reusable structures, few module types, low material and realistic manufacture, services and thermal interfaces. The available RD53 chip is fixed; the exact inventory variant is being clarified. Pixel volume/layer layout is not selected by this task.

The Tracking Engineer leads two independent alternatives, each with top-view and cross-section drawings, source facts/derivations/design choices and explicit limitations. The Project Coordinator supplies a balanced comparison and conditional recommendation after technical synthesis.

Public RD53 documentation and ATLAS/CMS detector/upgrade TDRs are references, not an instruction to copy either experiment. Catalogue every new normative source in reference/manifest.yaml, distinguish RD53A from production successors, and leave unverified thickness/power/irradiation assumptions visible. Include active/inactive area, chip tiling, bumps, flex/adhesive/bonds, sensor bias/isolation, material accounting and credible cooling/power/data handoffs. Layout fit, radiation requirements, engineering tolerances and production sign-off remain separate gates.

Scope: DRAFT designs and source/design study evidence only; no detector geometry or reconstruction changes. Update project tracking in the same PR. Existing context: stage B/C of PLAN-NODD-001, global envelope baseline DES-003 / ADR-006, with the formal-sign-off documentation discrepancy preserved.
